newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU summit recesses for Franco-German-Lux talks.
newsitem.headline: EU summit recesses for Franco-German-Lux talks.

text.p: A European Union summit went into recess on Friday while the leaders of Germany, France and Luxembourg met to resolve a dispute on a budget stability pact for countries joining a single currency, an EU diplomat said.
Luxembourg's Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker was offering a compromise proposal on budget discipline between the hardline position of Germany and the concerns of France, the diplomat said.
"Juncker, (President Jacques) Chirac and (Chancellor Helmut) Kohl have split off to discuss a compromise," the diplomat told Reuters.

The main stumbling block was Bonn's insistence that the exceptional circumstances that would justify breaching a budget deficit limit of three percent of gross domestic product would have to be a recession of at least one percent of GDP.

Juncker, who is also his country's finance minister, offered two options. One was that the one-percent limit should be tied to a clause specifying that EU finance ministers would have the ultimate political say in determining whether a country should be fined for overspending.
As an alternative, he suggested exceptional circumstances could be defined automatically as a recession of 0.75 percent of GDP, with no political decision required.
